why: No hyperscaler has cut 2027 plans, but cracks are showing. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says Google is cutting 2027 shipments of a Broadcom-designed AI chip by about a fifth (neither company has commented), and Alphabet sold bonds at wider spreads than in May. After the Democratic sweep, UBS says ~30% of expected 2028 US data-centre additions could be at risk from construction pauses. Spending is still debt-funded, with free cash flow negative at three of the four biggest spenders.

Nvidia jumped 31% on Monday to US$164.50 after its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, one of the largest one-day gains in market value on record. Micron rose about 19% and CoreWeave 22%. The rebound recovers only part of last week’s losses: Nvidia is still about a third below its October record, the board’s own investigation continues, and Reuters has reported SEC staff are examining possible accounting issues (no finding of wrongdoing). Rebounds of this size often follow sharp falls and do not by themselves end a sell-off.

A 25 bp hike on 9 Dec is still about 93–96% priced (CME FedWatch, 23 Nov), down from about 100% last week. Governor Cook says policy is not tight enough, while Treasury Secretary Bessent warned more tightening could be a mistake. October PCE inflation lands at 12:30am Thursday 26 Nov Melbourne time.

No newer default-swap figures have been published since Friday, when Oracle’s protection rose to about 328 bp (above the 300 bp bursting threshold) and CoreWeave’s to about 1,233 bp. Shares rebounded on Monday (CoreWeave +22%), so watch whether default protection eases too. ETFs that would bet against CoreWeave, Oracle and Meta debt have been filed with the SEC.

Anthropic traded around US$87–88 on Monday, slightly below Friday’s US$88.91 and still only about 5% above its US$83 IPO price, missing out on the AI rebound. It has committed about US$900bn to computing over two decades, and investors expect its debt to be rated below investment grade (no rating yet). Nvidia’s US$118bn of customer guarantees, about US$105bn tied to one OpenAI campus, remains in focus. (Disclosure: Claude is made by Anthropic.)
Edged up to about 4.94% on Monday (early afternoon) as money moved back into shares, after falling 13 bp on Friday. The bursting pattern of yields falling sharply while stocks fall paused on Monday.

US crude fell about 2.7% to around US$81 on Monday, extending a three-week losing streak; Brent was about US$92 in early trade. Oil is easing slightly but remains well above pre-war levels, keeping inflation pressure on the Fed.
High-yield spread 323 bp on 13 Nov (320 bp on 12 Nov): broad credit is still calm. IMF: US bank loans to non-bank lenders rose 18% in 2026.

Monday’s rebound was broad: the S&P 500 rose 4.8% (best day since April 2025), the Nasdaq 6.5%, the Dow 3.0% and small caps about 3%, and gold rose about 4%. It recovers roughly half of last week’s fall; the S&P 500 is still about 6% below its October record.
